exposure: maternal exposure to pesticides and chemicals during pregnancy
cohort: The study included 100 children aged 0-16 years (50 with cancer and 50 controls without cancer) from Sulaimani Hiwa Hospital and Pediatric Teaching Hospital.
finding: The study found that cesarean section, family history, maternal exposure to pesticides and chemicals during pregnancy, child exposure to pesticides, passive smoke, caffeine consumption, and fast food consumption were significantly linked to cancer in children.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as a risk factor for cancer in children (odds 2.7, P=0.02).
